C-CURRENT-VALIDATION-BOUNDARY-1-D8D7DF85.Summary: First small slice of the current-only CLI policy recorded in `CLAUDE.md:5` and confirmed by the withdrawn compatibility campaign in `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/grace-implementation-queue.md:154-156`. Automatic project validation and query-index inputs stop reading archived artifact contents: `validateNgraceProject` (root lint) and `loadGraceArtifactIndex` (module/context navigation) no longer open archived bundles, and `lintGraceProject` no longer discovers or extracts archived `plan.xml` assertions. Active and selected-current validation, graph/verification integrity, the `.ngrace` implementation-source exclusion, and pre-existing archive bytes are preserved. The explicit `--as <status>` preview and the shared single-artifact `validateChangeArtifact` are left intact, so a current `--as applied` validation of a selected artifact still works; retirement of explicit archived selection belongs to its own consumer slice. `README.md` and `examples/` are unchanged: the user-facing cutover, status/scope attribution, explicit archived navigation, historical reporting, and the apply/close transaction are separate dependent bundles. This overturns the unrelated-malformed-archive refusal and the archived spec-to-plan coverage rule recorded in `.ngrace/changes/archive/C-ARCHIVE-CORPUS-BASELINE-2-D5F2E1C3/spec.xml:211-241` and `src/artifact/grammar.ts:1474-1477`.

Goals.Goal: Make the automatic current project grammar stop opening archived spec, plan, companion, and design-context contents. In `src/artifact/grammar.ts` the archive location of `validateChangeBundlesInDirectory` inspects only directory-name identity (`C-*` name and unsupported loose `.xml` names); malformed XML, a differing `graceVersion`, missing required sections, unregistered sections, spec-to-plan coverage, companion content, and superseded replacement content in an archive bundle create no current grammar or coverage issue. Active-bundle grammar validation and active spec-to-plan coverage are unchanged.

Make automatic current lint stop discovering and parsing archived plan assertions. In `src/lint/core.ts` the archived-plan enumeration and its `BaselineAssertions` / `TargetAssertions` extraction are removed. Active approved-baseline evaluation under `--assertions current`, and the selected baseline, target, and final rules, are unchanged.

Make the query index automatic path current-only. In `src/query/core.ts`, `collectOperationalValidationErrors` reads active plans only; `loadGraceArtifactIndex`, module navigation, and the selected-active task slice stay readable and byte-identical under opaque unrelated archive content.

Preserve every guard that a broader archive boundary could silently disarm: active and selected-current refusal paths, graph and verification integrity, `.ngrace` code exclusion from implementation-source and query/context entries, directory-name archive identity checks, the explicit `--as` preview, and the bytes of every pre-existing archived bundle.

Preview boundary. Second, the archived spec-to-plan coverage rule in `src/artifact/grammar.ts:1474-1477` ("Run for active and archive: historical bundles that already match stay quiet; mismatches surface so archives remain truthful"; G-05 / Safeguard 5). Current schemas validate current work and the current close; old evidence is retained byte-for-byte without retroactive conformance enforcement, so a historical bundle whose spec and plan coverage no longer match today's schema is not a current issue. The active coverage check is retained. This is not `C-GRAPH-COVERAGE`'s GraphAnchors/OWS archive policy, which is a different rule and is not changed here. Neither predecessor record is revalidated and no archived fixture is edited.

A `CloseEvidence` command names the narrow instrument for its subject; `bun run validate:ci` is reserved for the one criterion genuinely about the whole suite. A `bun:test` `spyOn` wraps the real exported `readGraceXmlArtifact`, calls through to the original, and records each call's `file` argument; driving the real `validateNgraceProject` over a complete ordinary project yields an empty set of recorded calls whose path is under `.ngrace/changes/archive/` and a non-empty set of current-artifact calls as the positive control; the spy is restored after each test and no fake parser, monkey-patched return, or fabricated result is used. A test selectable by `-t "current grammar treats archive content as opaque"` in `src/artifact/grammar.test.ts` carries this.

C-CURRENT-VALIDATION-BOUNDARY-1-D8D7DF85.Problem: The maintainer's policy states that CLI determinism serves current project state, active changes and implementation, and the bundle being closed, while older archives are passive historical evidence (`CLAUDE.md:5`). Today the automatic path does the opposite. Three readers open archived XML on every root lint and every navigation: `src/artifact/grammar.ts:1353-1355` runs `validateChangeBundlesInDirectory` over `paths.changesArchiveDir`, and the archive branch at `src/artifact/grammar.ts:1424-1504` parses archived spec, plan, and companion files and runs current specification, section, and spec-to-plan coverage checks; `src/lint/core.ts:544-547` and `src/lint/core.ts:727-729` separately enumerate archived `plan.xml` files and extract their assertions; and `src/query/core.ts:93-99` reads active **and** archive plan assertions while `src/query/core.ts:127-146` builds the query index that module navigation and the selected-active context slice consume. The result, reproduced against the real CLI, is that a malformed, differently versioned, or section-incomplete unrelated archive bundle makes `ngrace lint`, `ngrace module find`, and `ngrace context --task` fail with codes such as `xml.parse` and `change.applied-plan-missing`, so historical format drift drives current operational results. This bundle removes archive contents from the automatic validation and query-index paths while preserving every active, selected-current, identity, projection, exclusion, preview, and byte-preservation guard. It is deliberately narrow: status/scope attribution, explicit archived navigation, historical reporting, post-archive verdict evaluation, and the apply/close transaction still read archives and require their own dependent bundles, and those consumers are expected to inherit the shared validator's new current-only behaviour rather than a permanent exception. It overturns two archived-bundle rules. First, the unrelated-malformed-archive refusal that `C-ARCHIVE-CORPUS-BASELINE-2-D5F2E1C3` preserved as the counterweight to excluding `.ngrace` scratch code; the exclusion and all guards survive, so the counterweight's purpose is met by a current-only rather than a whole-corpus validator. Second, the archived spec-to-plan coverage rule at `src/artifact/grammar.ts:1474-1477`, which kept historical bundles "truthful" by re-running current coverage over them (G-05 / Safeguard 5); current schemas validate current work and the current close, so old evidence is retained without retroactive conformance enforcement, while active coverage is preserved. This is not `C-GRAPH-COVERAGE`'s GraphAnchors/OWS archive policy. The explicit preview is untouched: `--as applied` computes its validator location from the requested virtual status (`src/lint/core.ts:134-136`), so it can validate a selected current artifact under archive-status rules and remains intact.

If a receipt has expired, the same behaviour is reproduced on a throwaway fixture before it is cited.
